<thought>From the ESI‑MS spectrum the most intense ion is at m/z 233.9632, which corresponds to the protonated molecule [M+H]⁺. Subtracting the mass of a proton (1.007276 Da) gives a neutral monoisotopic mass of ≈ 232.956 Da. The isotopic pattern shows a strong M+2 peak (~24 % of the base), characteristic of a single chlorine atom (Cl‑35/Cl‑37). Removing the monoisotopic mass of Cl‑35 (34.968853 Da) leaves 197.987 Da to be accounted for by C, H and O atoms. The combination C₁₁H₂O₄ matches this remaining mass within 3 ppm (exact mass 197.987 Da). Adding the chlorine atom yields the molecular formula C₁₁H₂O₄Cl, which fits the observed exact mass and isotopic distribution.  

Thus the molecular formula of the compound is: C11H2O4Cl.
